lead.headline: India clears ₹14,500 crore subsidy to build 92 GWh of grid storage by 2030-31
signal: If bids keep clearing at falling prices, storage turns solar into evening power and cuts discoms' costly peak purchases.
The 40% rule is a test: if domestic cell supply lags, projects stall or the rule is diluted.
lead.hook: The Cabinet approved a ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF, a subsidy that closes a project's cost gap) scheme to build ==92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage== by 2030-31.
points: Total investment is expected at ₹97,600 crore, so each rupee of subsidy pulls in close to seven rupees. The new capacity equals 170% of today's grid-scale storage.
The mix is 60 GWh of pumped storage (water pumped uphill, released through turbines), 30 GWh of batteries and 2 GWh of emerging technologies.

Why now: India's peak demand comes after dark when solar output is zero. Surplus noon power is wasted and coal covers the evening. The Central Electricity Authority says India needs about 411 GWh by 2031-32.
Battery storage prices found in bidding fell from about ₹10.18 per kWh in 2022-23 to around ₹2.1 per kWh by December 2025, without VGF and assuming two cycles a day.

All battery projects need 40% domestic content. This creates demand for Indian cells, packs and inverters, alongside the ₹18,100 crore PLI (production-linked incentive) scheme targeting 50 GWh of domestic cell manufacturing.

Capacity is awarded through competitive bidding, with distribution companies (discoms) eligible. __Execution risk sits in pumped-storage clearances and in meeting the 40% rule while domestic cell capacity is still being built.__
lead.editors_read: Subsidy plus a local-content rule plus a cell-manufacturing incentive is a deliberate attempt to avoid the solar-module pattern, where imports filled the gap. The binding constraint is now cell supply and pumped-storage construction time, not money. Developers of pumped storage and Indian cell makers gain most if bids are timely.
lead.evidence_of: Storage is becoming the bottleneck for clean power

frontpage.headline: AI system running an unreleased Anthropic model claims proof of a 2008 quantum conjecture
signal: If the proof holds, quantum pitches for messy, unstructured business data lose their strongest argument, a useful filter for hype.
frontpage.hook: US startup PSI says its AI system, running an unreleased Anthropic model, ==proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture==, open since about 2008, and that Lean (a proof checker) accepted it.
points: The proof says that for yes-or-no questions on random, patternless data, an ordinary computer can predict a quantum computer's answer without exponentially more reads of the data.
PSI says the system produced the proof on day three of a run, then improved its own result twice on related problems. The paper and formal proof are on GitHub.
Known exponential quantum speedups, such as Shor's factoring, depend on hidden structure in the input. Anyone promising exponential gains on unstructured data must now say where the pattern is.

Earlier bounds for general polynomials shrank exponentially with degree, too weak to rule out such speedups. The paper is not peer-reviewed, and neither Aaronson nor Ambainis had commented as of 7 November.
frontpage.editors_read: The quantum result matters less than the method: a proof a machine checks step by step removes the need to trust the author. Peer review and expert reaction are the next test. Separately today, Anthropic's generator deal shows the same labs are also scaling physical infrastructure.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI is starting to settle open research problems

frontpage.headline: Iraq says it has US understandings to export oil through Hormuz
signal: If exports flow, it eases supply pressure on oil, a big gain for import-dependent India.
frontpage.hook: Iraq has reached understandings with the United States to allow Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz via a shipping lane near Oman, Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said.
points: Hussein made the remarks in an interview with Al Jazeera, per Reuters coverage.
The available text gives no volumes, dates or terms of the arrangement.
frontpage.editors_read: Reasoning beyond the text: Iraq depends on Gulf shipping for most of its oil revenue, so a negotiated lane is worth more to Baghdad than any single market move. Details are thin, so treat it as intent, not flow. Separately today, Brent fell about 13% on de-escalation hopes.
frontpage.evidence_of: Oil and the Iran conflict are driving markets

frontpage.headline: Cop31 opens in Turkey with the US absent and an El Niño at record strength
signal: If the Iran war keeps fossil fuels expensive, the economic case for electrification strengthens even without US backing.
frontpage.hook: Delegates from close to 190 countries open Cop31 in Antalya, Turkey, amid the ==strongest El Niño on record==, with the US sending no delegation for a second year.
points: Turkey hosts, but Australia presides over negotiations after a compromise on rival bids. Australia's Chris Bowen wants a tangible outcome on implementation of emissions cuts and finance.
Rich and poor countries are expected to clash over who pays for climate impacts. Bowen says only 0.2% of climate finance goes to small island states for adaptation.
Temperatures have passed the 1.5C Paris limit this year. This summer more than 50,000 people died in Europe's heatwaves, and a Nepal glacier collapse caused over 1,500 deaths.
On the table: a target for 35% of global final energy to come from electricity by 2035, which faces opposition from some countries.
Both presiding countries rely on fossil fuels, and Australia is a top coal and LNG exporter. Twenty US Democratic members of Congress are attending.
frontpage.evidence_of: Fossil-fuel shocks are strengthening the case for electrification

frontpage.headline: Bangladesh says it has asked India to extradite Sheikh Hasina
signal: If India holds out, expect continued friction with a government that is now elected, not interim.
frontpage.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
frontpage.hook: Bangladesh's law minister called ousted PM Sheikh Hasina a "convicted criminal" and said Dhaka has formally requested her ==extradition from India== under the bilateral treaty.
points: Hasina fled to India on August 5, 2024 after a mass uprising ended her 15-year rule.
In November 2025, a tribunal tried her in absentia and sentenced her to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another for crimes against humanity.
The BNP, led by Tarique Rahman, formed government after February elections.
India has acknowledged the requests but announced no decision, saying they are being examined.
Hasina said in August she intended to return in December; Dhaka was "outraged" at her press conference.
frontpage.evidence_of: South Asian politics is tangling with neighbour relations

frontpage.headline: Delhi PM2.5 passes 50 times WHO limit after Deepavali firecracker ban is ignored
signal: Bans without enforcement did not hold, so expect the festive spike to compound the seasonal one.
frontpage.source: India Latest News: Top National Headlines Today & Breaking News | The Hindu
frontpage.hook: PM2.5 hit ==767 micrograms per cubic metre at Anand Vihar== at 11 p.m., about 51 times the WHO's 15 limit, after firecrackers continued past the Supreme Court's 10 p.m. deadline.
points: Akshardham read 760.99 (about 50.7 times the limit) and Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium 702 (about 46.8 times), per DPCC data.
PM2.5 is fine particles that enter the lungs and bloodstream and cause respiratory and other diseases.
Delhi's overall air stayed "very poor", with parts "severe".
Winter pollution rises on low winds and cooler temperatures, with stubble burning and firecrackers adding to vehicle and dust emissions.
frontpage.evidence_of: Rules on pollution are not being enforced

frontpage.headline: India's hiring is up 14%, but software engineering is up only 1%
signal: If the pattern holds, AI, data and domain-heavy roles are where the 14% sits, not generic coding.
The November index in early December is the first clean comparison.
frontpage.hook: White-collar hiring rose 14% in October, but ==software engineering and QA hiring rose just 1%==, per the Naukri JobSpeak Index.
points: The index stood at 2,836 against 2,480 a year earlier, but fell from 3,053 in September. Diwali fell in October 2025, depressing last year's base.
Growth was in production (39%), automobiles (36%, R&D 53%), AI and machine learning (32%) and global capability centres (18%).
IT and software services hiring rose 5%. An ICRIER survey of 651 IT firms found close to two-thirds class developers as significantly exposed to AI.
Professionals with 13 to 16 years and 16+ years of experience each saw 22% growth, against 15% for freshers.
Hyderabad led metros at 15%; Kolkata was flat.
frontpage.evidence_of: Indian hiring is splitting into specialist and generic

frontpage.headline: Anthropic buys $3.4 billion of gas generator capacity for data centres
signal: If grid connections stay slow, AI labs will build their own power, adding gas demand.
frontpage.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News
frontpage.hook: Anthropic struck a deal worth about $3.4 billion for ==1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators== from OnePWR Solutions, the Financial Times reported.
points: It bought the commitments in late September. It did not acquire OnePWR, but the deal included engineering and construction capability to install the units.
Reuters could not verify the report, and neither company commented.
Reuters reported in September that Anthropic __expects to spend more than $500 billion over 10__ years on AI infrastructure.
Claude demand is pushing the company to secure more computing and power.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI spending is straining power, markets and security

stories.headline: Nvidia board opens probe after CEO Jensen Huang admits infidelity
signal: If the probe finds a leak, pressure on Nvidia's already limited China licences would rise.
stories.hook: Nvidia's board is investigating whether CEO Jensen Huang, 63, was ==targeted by a foreign espionage plot== after he admitted to employees he was unfaithful to his wife.
points: The probe will be run by a committee of independent directors with outside counsel. Huang stays CEO pending the results.
Reports say a former Megaspeed International executive, whom the US government suspects was recruited by a Chinese spy agency, targeted him. Megaspeed is accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to China.
The board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.
Nvidia has no public succession plan. Its market cap hit nearly $5.8 trillion in October and has slipped below $5 trillion. It reports earnings later this month.
stories.evidence_of: AI spending is straining power, markets and security

stories.headline: Foreign investors put ₹46,000 crore into Indian shares in five sessions as AI stocks fall
signal: India's flows now depend on oil and US rates more than on its own earnings.
stories.hook: Foreign portfolio investors bought ₹45,970 crore of Indian equities in five sessions, and the ==Nifty 50 rose 8.6%==, its best week since February 2021.
points: This reverses two months of net selling. The Nifty is still down 4.21% for the year, and the rupee rose 0.6% to 93.91 per dollar, its strongest since April.
Brent fell about 13% to roughly $98 on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation, the biggest weekly drop since the start of Covid, easing inflation and the current account.
A tech rout took the Nasdaq down 5.5% on Thursday, on weak Qualcomm results and fears of slowing AI spending. India has little AI exposure, so funds rotated in.
Watch US CPI data due Tuesday, with a December US rate hike nearly priced in. __A hot reading or Brent back above $100 could end the inflows.__
stories.evidence_of: Money is rotating from AI trades into India

stories.headline: Apple's new CEO pushes to turn Siri into an autonomous agent
signal: If Apple ships an agent, it competes with OpenAI and Anthropic on the device itself.
stories.hook: Apple's new CEO is pressing software chief Craig Federighi to take a more ambitious AI approach, aiming to turn Siri into an agent that can get things done for users.
points: Bloomberg's newsletter also says Apple is shaking up its development strategy for iOS 28.
The new MacBook Pro goes on sale (summary from limited source text).
stories.evidence_of: Big platforms are moving from chatbots to AI agents

stories.headline: Fridge hacks, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist raise fears of a hacking surge
signal: If AI keeps finding flaws faster than owners patch them, old connected devices become the weak point.
stories.hook: Three attacks in days, including a ==$6.3bn theft from Binance==, led the UK's cyber chief to say we are in the "foothills" of a new hacking landscape.
points: Fridge controllers across Europe were hit, with some units reaching 50C. The fault was old, unpatched equipment and default passwords published in manuals, not AI.
On 30 October Binance lost $6.3bn, attributed to North Korea. On 1 November hackers sent Kyiv residents a fake nuclear alert via Ukraine's emergency app.
Since Anthropic released Mythos in April, vulnerabilities found by leading tech companies rose eight-fold. But one expert says the surge in flaws has not become a surge in breaches.
The NCSC says AI-powered malware is "highly likely" to hit UK power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028. Ex-NCSC head Ciaran Martin calls this a bad wave, not unprecedented.
stories.evidence_of: AI is speeding up discovery of security flaws

also.line: Richard Sutton, who wrote 2019's "The Bitter Lesson", argues in a new post that compute alone is not enough for intelligence and AI science is "far from finished".
DeepSeek says its AI agent platform has 1.54 million daily users, as the Chinese firm continues to challenge Anthropic and OpenAI with agent applications.

stories.headline: IEA: India's renewables to hit 530 GW by 2030
signal: Separately today, the ₹14,500 crore storage scheme targets one of these constraints directly.
stories.hook: The IEA projects India's renewable capacity at ==about 530 GW by 2030==, with solar PV over 80% of the growth, making it the second-largest renewable growth market.
points: Capacity has crossed 300 GW, nearly four times a decade ago. By 2030 solar is forecast above 350 GW, wind near 90 GW and hydro 75 GW.
Annual additions should stay above 50 GW, against 49 GW in 2025, and could reach 70 GW in a faster scenario.
Renewable generation should nearly double from about 500 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh, lifting its share from nearly 25% to 35%.
The IEA names transmission delays, too little storage, land acquisition, project delays and weak discom finances as the constraints. __Fixing them could lift 2026-2030 additions by more than 20%.__
stories.evidence_of: Storage is becoming the bottleneck for clean power

also.line: US solar maker First Solar is investing another $150 million in India on top of $700 million already invested, nearing $1 billion cumulative; CEO Mark Widmar called for policy clarity.

stories.headline: Blood test matches MRI-based method for staging liver disease
signal: If it is validated further, a blood draw could replace scarce imaging for deciding who gets MASH treatment.
stories.source: Top Health News | Latest Healthcare Sector & Healthcare Industry news, Information and Updates: ET HealthWorld : ETHealthworld.com
stories.hook: Hepta's LiquidTransformer blood test staged liver damage from MASH (a fatty-liver disease with inflammation and scarring) ==nearly as accurately as magnetic resonance elastography (MRE)==, researchers reported at the AASLD meeting.
points: Staging MASH today needs MRE, mostly at specialist centres, or a liver biopsy. Existing blood tests cannot stage it.
The test reads DNA circulating in blood. With Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, researchers showed it identified patients eligible for Rezdiffra, the first approved MASH drug.
Across six presentations it beat second-line options: an ultrasound method and the enhanced liver fibrosis blood test.

Separately, Ipsen's Iqirvo normalised a liver enzyme (ALP) in 85.3% of 92 primary biliary cholangitis patients at one year, against 23.3% on placebo. An editorial says benefit to long-term outcomes is not yet shown.
stories.evidence_of: Blood tests are replacing imaging for diagnosis

also.line: India's pharma exports grew 4.9% year-on-year to $16.14 billion in the first half of FY27, helped by shipments to Europe, ASEAN and Latin America despite trade tensions.

stories.headline: Fewer monsoon depressions are shifting India's rain south
signal: If the trend continues, crop and water planning in central and eastern India faces less reliable monsoon rain.
stories.hook: Monsoon depressions over the Bay of Bengal ==fell from 26 in the 1980s to 10 in 2010-2020==, shifting rain away from eastern and central India toward the southern peninsula.
points: Depressions are low-pressure systems that bring days of widespread rain. The sharpest decline is in August, when they usually peak.
Cause: the equatorial Indian Ocean and western Pacific have warmed more than the northern Bay of Bengal. That weakened the Walker and Hadley circulations, so fewer winds converge over the Bay.
Rain fell along the usual paths, especially central India and the Gangetic plains, while parts of the peninsula got more.
The researchers say agriculture, groundwater recharge and water supplies in dependent regions could be affected.
stories.evidence_of: Climate change is shifting where India's rain falls

stories.headline: Angel One becomes India's second-largest broker by active clients
signal: If retail trading volumes keep rising, the active-client gap between the top three narrows to a race.
stories.hook: Angel One has ==69.98 lakh active NSE clients==, 14.97% of the 4.67 crore total, overtaking Zerodha for second place.
points: It added 2.43 lakh active clients in October. Groww leads with 1.37 crore (29.43% share) and added 3.04 lakh.
Zerodha fell to third with 67.59 lakh, down 32,435 from September, and a 14.46% share.
Angel One's total client base reached 4.06 crore, up 17.4% year on year. Average daily orders rose 19.6% month on month to 69.7 lakh.
Its revenue rose 18.7% to ₹1,427 crore and net profit rose 58.2% to ₹335 crore.
stories.evidence_of: Retail investing is consolidating among a few brokers

also.line: Twenty Indian startups raised $255 million between November 2 and 6, per Inc42: up 96% from $130.3 million the previous week, while deal count fell 38% from 32.

stories.headline: Zipline raises $1.5 billion at $21.5 billion valuation
signal: If the FAA's proposed Part 108 rule lands, routine beyond-line-of-sight flights could replace the waiver process.
stories.hook: US drone delivery firm Zipline raised ==$1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation==, nearly three times its $7.6 billion valuation from earlier this year.
points: Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led. Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, Fidelity, ARK and Salesforce Ventures also took part.
The money goes to US manufacturing and hiring for a nationwide network. Walmart __will launch 300 more sites__, and Uber targets one million deliveries a day by 2029.

The CEO says Zipline built much of its technology and manufacturing itself because no drone supply chain existed, and it launched abroad first because beyond-line-of-sight flights were illegal in the US.

The company claims 150 million autonomous miles with zero safety incidents. Regulatory approvals and noise concerns remain barriers, and Amazon plans to grow from 11 locations to about 500 by year-end.
stories.evidence_of: Capital is moving into physical-world robotics

stories.headline: Gita Gopinath expects AI correction, warns of US recession risk
signal: If AI spending slows, AI-supply-chain economies like Taiwan and Korea are most exposed.
stories.hook: Former IMF chief economist Gita Gopinath says ==a market correction in AI is likely==, as companies may struggle to earn back the nearly $1 trillion being invested in 2026.
points: She cannot say when. She calls the setup a gamble: the AI boom supports growth while tariffs, geopolitics and the US-Iran conflict weigh on it.
Taiwan and South Korea are growing at about twice their usual pace; Taiwan has raised its 2026 __forecast to 11.05%__, its fastest since 1987. Gulf economies face downgrades.
Circular funding is a risk: Nvidia invests in AI labs, which use the money to buy Nvidia chips, so one failure could spread.
A sharp stock fall could push US growth to zero or slightly negative, though a market-driven recession would likely be short.
stories.evidence_of: AI spending is straining power, markets and security

stories.headline: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses outside power, runs on diesel generators
signal: If neither line is restored within the fuel window, risk rises; watch for another IAEA-brokered repair pause.
stories.hook: Europe's largest nuclear plant lost its off-site electricity after the Ferosplavna line disconnected, and has ==fuel for about two weeks== of limited emergency generator use, the IAEA says.
points: The plant makes no power but needs external supply to keep fuel cool. The cause of the disconnection is unknown.
The main Dniprovska line was already unavailable as of October 23.
An IAEA-brokered local ceasefire in early September allowed repairs after an outage from August 20.
Russian-installed management says the line shut by automatic protection and radiation levels are normal.
stories.evidence_of: War is repeatedly knocking out critical infrastructure

stories.headline: Modi says armed Maoists are gone, warns of 'dimagi Naxals' in parties and groups
signal: The label has no legal definition, so watch whether it is used to target specific parties or groups.
stories.source: India Latest News: Top National Headlines Today & Breaking News | The Hindu
stories.hook: Speaking at a CRPF camp in Bastar, PM Modi said armed Maoists have been eliminated but =="dimagi Naxals" (ideological supporters)== have infiltrated parties and organisations.
points: The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026. At the peak, over 230 districts across nearly 20 states were affected, with about 2,000 attacks a year.
He said no CRPF personnel died in the line of duty over the past year, the first time in 47 years.
He credited cutting off funding, the counterfeit currency nexus and supply of weapons, and freeing security forces to act.
He made a similar remark on Independence Day in August; he named no groups.
stories.evidence_of: Political rhetoric is shifting from armed to ideological threats

stories.headline: Ten years after demonetisation, cash use is where it started
signal: Digital payments won on convenience, not by forcing cash out of the economy.
stories.hook: Currency held by the public was ==12.1% of GDP in March 2026==, against 11.9% before demonetisation in 2015-16, despite the UPI boom.
points: The move invalidated 86% of currency by value. The RBI's 2017-18 report said ₹15.31 lakh crore of ₹15.42 lakh crore returned (99.3%), undercutting the black-money goal.
UPI accounted for 85% of payment transactions by volume in 2025 but only 9.5% by value. Smartphones and the pandemic also drove the shift.
Counterfeits detected per crore notes fell from 70.1 to 13.4, but counterfeit ₹500 notes rose from 0.3 to 20.1.
Independent estimates put output loss at 1% to 2.5% of GDP in 2016-17. About 85% of Indian workers are in informal enterprises.
stories.evidence_of: Digital payments grew without displacing cash

stories.headline: Microsoft opens fourth India cloud region in Hyderabad
signal: If that growth materialises, power and land become the constraints on India's AI buildout, as with Anthropic's generator deal elsewhere today.
stories.hook: Microsoft launched its India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad, its ==fourth in India==, after Pune, Chennai and Mumbai.
points: It is part of Microsoft's previously announced $20.5 billion India investment.
Microsoft India's president says India generates nearly 20% of the world's data but has only about 3% of data centre capacity.
India has about 2 GW of data centre capacity, expected to reach 12-14 GW by 2035.
stories.evidence_of: AI spending is straining power, markets and security

stories.headline: Sudan's army detains ICC-wanted ex-ruling party chief Ahmed Haroun
signal: Whether he is handed to the ICC is not stated (summary from limited source text).
stories.hook: Sudan's army detained Ahmed Haroun, chairman of the former ruling National Congress Party, who is ==charged by the ICC with more than 40 counts== of war crimes and crimes against humanity.
points: Two party officials told Reuters of the detention on Sunday.
Haroun served under ousted strongman Omar al-Bashir.
stories.evidence_of: Accountability for past regimes is resurfacing

stories.headline: India's 'Cockroach Janta Party' youth movement targets the election commissioner
signal: Youth jobs and exam integrity are now a political force with a track record of results.
stories.source: Al Jazeera – Breaking News, World News and Video from Al Jazeera
stories.hook: The Cockroach Janta Party, a youth movement that began as online satire, says it aims to restore accountability, and ==weeks after its May launch the education minister resigned==.
points: It mobilised thousands against exam paper leaks, unemployment and the high cost of living.

Protesters now want the chief election commissioner out. Opposition parties and the group accuse the commission of manipulating voter lists to favour the BJP; the commission denies it and says it removed dead, duplicate and ineligible voters.
The BJP accuses demonstrators of sowing chaos. Several CJP leaders, including founder Abhijeet Dipke's guest on the programme, have been arrested.
stories.evidence_of: Young Indians are organising politically over jobs and exams

stories.headline: Cheap 3D-printed, drone-dropped mines are back in Ukraine
signal: Cheap, simple weapons raise decades-long civilian risk in any conflict zone.
stories.hook: Antipersonnel mines are returning 29 years after 122 countries signed the Ottawa Treaty, enabled by ==3D printing, microcontrollers and drone delivery==.
points: Frontline units can print their own mines in varied shapes that blend into vegetation or look like brick.

Microcontroller sensors, such as magnetic, Doppler microwave, heat or Bluetooth triggers, replace tripwires. Drones place mines precisely on paths and around trenches, and a UN commission reports Russia drops them to target civilians in Kherson.
Poland, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia are leaving the Ottawa Treaty; Ukraine suspended its implementation.
Expert Seán Moorhouse expects the technology to spread worldwide and says demining agencies must adapt.
stories.evidence_of: Cheap tech is reshaping modern warfare

stories.headline: Sleep disorders linked to changes in attention-related brain regions
signal: Brain markers could someday support earlier diagnosis, but cause is not yet established.
stories.hook: A meta-analysis of ==57 brain imaging studies== links sleep disorders to reductions in the thalamus, a region central to attention and thinking.
points: Both dyssomnias (insomnia, sleep apnea) and parasomnias (sleepwalking, nightmares) were tied to changes in the pulvinar, a part of the thalamus that directs attention.
Parasomnias also showed changes in the posterior cingulate cortex, involved in motivation and emotion. No pattern was found exclusive to dyssomnias.
It shows association only. It cannot say whether poor sleep causes the changes, the reverse, or both.
stories.evidence_of: Brain imaging is revealing links across disorders

stories.headline: Experiment shows a space-time limit on tracking electrons
signal: The near-term use is lab tools for steering chemical reactions, not faster chips.
stories.hook: Regensburg and Max Planck researchers showed that ==an electron's timing and spatial spread trade off==: pinning down when it moves needs more energy, which spreads its wave packet in space.
points: Laser pulses drove electrons across a few atomic diameters from a metal tip to a silver surface, in an attosecond-scale experiment (an attosecond is a billionth of a billionth of a second).
Simulations found the electrons lagged the light field by about 500 attoseconds.
Even so, the wave packets stayed localised enough for atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The team says the insight could one day let electronics run hundreds of thousands of times faster than CMOS, but this is a long-term goal, not demonstrated.
stories.evidence_of: Experiments are probing quantum limits of electrons

also.line: New Journal of Neuroscience research suggests lifelong-blind people hear pitch better because their auditory systems process sounds more consistently, pointing to internal noise as a key factor.

stories.headline: 52% of Indian CEOs plan some job cuts, 92% expect headcount to grow
signal: Roles get rewritten rather than removed overall; entry-level definitions are the first to change.
stories.hook: KPMG's survey of 125 Indian CEOs finds ==52% plan workforce cuts in some areas==, up from 50% in 2025, while 92% expect total headcount to grow over three years.
points: 78% call AI a top investment priority (79% globally). 62% __expect to put 11-20% of budgets into AI__, and about 70% expect returns in one to three years.
86% are reviewing skills required for entry-level roles, against 76% globally. 87% are prioritising retaining and retraining high-potential staff, up from 70%.
46% say agentic AI (software that carries out tasks with some autonomy) is already having a significant impact, against 55% globally.
Barriers: ethics (64%) and inconsistent regional AI rules (53% vs 41% globally). Cybersecurity is the top threat to growth, at 38%.
stories.evidence_of: Indian hiring is splitting into specialist and generic

stories.headline: AI, data and cybersecurity make up 30.3% of GCC tech hiring demand
signal: Scarce skills carry the premium; a supply gap that large favours people who can retrain into AI and data.
stories.hook: AI, data and cybersecurity skills reached ==30.3% of tech hiring demand== at India's global capability centres (GCCs) in July-September, up from 25.8%, even as overall demand fell 3.5%.
points: AI, data and analytics demand grew about 14% quarter on quarter; cybersecurity and __risk rose 12%__.
The report estimates talent supply gaps of 38-42% in AI, data and analytics, and 30-35% in cybersecurity.
Tier-2 cities grew 13% and now hold about 14% of hiring, led by Coimbatore at 30%. Bengaluru is still the largest, at 22.6%.
India has an estimated 2,250-2,400 GCCs, up 5-6%, and the workforce is projected to reach 2.7-2.8 million by 2030.
stories.evidence_of: Indian hiring is splitting into specialist and generic

opportunities.name: Top Business Schools Present: Application Tips (Virtual)
opportunities.summary: Admissions teams from ten MBA programmes, including Booth, Harvard, Stanford, Wharton, Kellogg, MIT Sloan and Columbia, share application tips. Online; link shared on registration.
